claim: Perirenal adipose tissue (PRAT) is a unique visceral depot that contains a mixture of brown and white adipocytes.
source: Perirenal adipose tissue (PRAT) is a unique visceral depot that contains a mixture of brown and white adipocytes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of PRAT.

claim: A distinct subpopulation of Ucp1-&Cidea+ adipocytes arises from brown-to-white conversion during postnatal life in the periureter region of mouse PRAT.
source: Here, we combine single-nucleus RNA sequencing with genetic lineage tracing to reveal the existence of a distinct subpopulation of Ucp1-&Cidea+ adipocytes that arises from brown-to-white conversion during postnatal life in the periureter region of mouse PRAT.
evidence: The claim is supported by snRNA-seq data and genetic lineage tracing experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cold exposure restores Ucp1 expression and a thermogenic phenotype in the Ucp1-&Cidea+ adipocyte subpopulation.
source: Cold exposure restores Ucp1 expression and a thermogenic phenotype in this subpopulation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing Ucp1 expression changes after cold exposure.

claim: The Ucp1-&Cidea+ adipocyte subpopulation has a transcriptome that is distinct from subcutaneous beige adipocytes.
source: These cells have a transcriptome that is distinct from subcutaneous beige adipocytes and may represent a unique type of cold-recruitable adipocytes.
evidence: This is supported by transcriptomic comparison data presented in the manuscript.

claim: White adipocytes contain a single large lipid droplet that occupies most of their intracellular space.
source: Being the most abundant type of adipocyte, white adipocytes (WAs) contain a single large lipid droplet that occupies most of their intracellular space.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about white adipocyte morphology.

claim: White adipocytes are present in visceral and subcutaneous depots.
source: They are present in visceral and subcutaneous depots and their primary function is to store excess energy in the form of triglycerides.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about white adipocyte distribution.

claim: The primary function of white adipocytes is to store excess energy in the form of triglycerides.
source: They are present in visceral and subcutaneous depots and their primary function is to store excess energy in the form of triglycerides.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about white adipocyte function.

claim: White adipocytes secrete hormones including leptin, adiponectin, and several others that regulate the function of other cells in adipose tissue as well as other organs.
source: WAs also secrete a number of hormones, including leptin, adiponectin, and several others, that regulate the function of other cells in adipose tissue as well as other organs (Scheja and Heeren, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Brown adipocytes contain numerous small lipid droplets and a high density of mitochondria.
source: In contrast, brown adipocytes (BAs) contain numerous small lipid droplets and a high density of mitochondria.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about brown adipocyte morphology.

claim: The primary function of brown adipocytes is the generation of heat through thermogenesis.
source: Their primary function is the generation of heat, that is, thermogenesis, through uncoupling of the mitochondrial electron transport chain from ATP production to produce heat.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about brown adipocyte function.

claim: Thermogenesis in brown adipocytes is mediated by uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1), a BA-specific protein located at the inner mitochondrial membrane.
source: This is mediated by uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1), a BA-specific protein located at the inner mitochondrial membrane (Cohen and Kajimura, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Beige adipocytes are residents of subcutaneous white adipose tissue depots that possess inducible thermogenic capacity.
source: Beige adipocytes (BeAs) are residents of subcutaneous white adipose tissue (WAT) depots that possess inducible thermogenic capacity, despite very low basal levels of UCP1 expression (Petrovic et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Beige adipocytes have very low basal levels of UCP1 expression.
source: Beige adipocytes (BeAs) are residents of subcutaneous white adipose tissue (WAT) depots that possess inducible thermogenic capacity, despite very low basal levels of UCP1 expression (Petrovic et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: snRNA-seq analysis of mouse and human WAT depots has revealed adipocyte subpopulations that are related to lipogenesis, lipid-scavenging, and stress responses.
source: snRNA-seq analysis of mouse and human WAT depots has revealed adipocyte subpopulations that are related to lipogenesis, lipid-scavenging, and stress responses (Emont et al., 2022; Sárvári et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Profiling of adipocytes from interscapular brown adipose tissue of mouse and human has identified a subpopulation that negatively regulates thermogenesis via paracrine secretion of acetate.
source: Profiling of adipocytes from interscapular brown adipose tissue (iBAT) of mouse and human has identified a subpopulation that negatively regulates thermogenesis via paracrine secretion of acetate (Sun et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Visceral depots such as epididymal, mesenteric, and retroperitoneal adipose tissues are mainly made of white adipocytes.
source: Visceral depots such as epididymal, mesenteric, and retroperitoneal adipose tissues are mainly made of WAs; whereas BAs and BeAs are often found in subcutaneous depots, such as iBAT and inguinal WAT (iWAT).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about adipose tissue distribution.

claim: Brown adipocytes and beige adipocytes are often found in subcutaneous depots, such as iBAT and inguinal WAT.
source: Visceral depots such as epididymal, mesenteric, and retroperitoneal adipose tissues are mainly made of WAs; whereas BAs and BeAs are often found in subcutaneous depots, such as iBAT and inguinal WAT (iWAT).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about adipose tissue distribution.

claim: Perirenal adipose tissue is bilaterally distributed around the kidney and is encapsulated by a multilayered fibrous membrane, known as the renal fascia.
source: Perirenal adipose tissue (PRAT) is bilaterally distributed around the kidney and is encapsulated by a multilayered fibrous membrane, known as the renal fascia (de Jong et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The medial region of PRAT is located around the hilum of the kidney.
source: The medial region of PRAT (herein termed mPRAT) is located around the hilum of the kidney, and several studies have identified UCP1-expressing BAs in this area in human PRAT, suggesting that it represents a form of visceral BAT (Betz et al., 2013; Li et al., 2015; Nagano et al., 2015; Svensson et al., 2014; van den Beukel et al., 2015; Vergnes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the anatomical location of mPRAT.

claim: Several studies have identified UCP1-expressing brown adipocytes in the medial region of human PRAT.
source: The medial region of PRAT (herein termed mPRAT) is located around the hilum of the kidney, and several studies have identified UCP1-expressing BAs in this area in human PRAT, suggesting that it represents a form of visceral BAT (Betz et al., 2013; Li et al., 2015; Nagano et al., 2015; Svensson et al., 2014; van den Beukel et al., 2015; Vergnes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The medial region of PRAT represents a form of visceral BAT.
source: The medial region of PRAT (herein termed mPRAT) is located around the hilum of the kidney, and several studies have identified UCP1-expressing BAs in this area in human PRAT, suggesting that it represents a form of visceral BAT (Betz et al., 2013; Li et al., 2015; Nagano et al., 2015; Svensson et al., 2014; van den Beukel et al., 2015; Vergnes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on cited studies showing UCP1-expressing BAs in this region.

claim: The lateral region of PRAT is predominantly composed of white adipocytes.
source: In contrast, the lateral region of PRAT (herein termed lPRAT) is predominantly composed of WAs (de Jong et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A process of continuous replacement of brown adipocytes by white adipocytes has been proposed based on morphological changes in adipocytes of human PRAT during aging.
source: Based on morphological changes in adipocytes of human PRAT during aging, a process of continuous replacement of BAs by WAs has been proposed (Tanuma et al., 1976; Tanuma et al., 1975).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Analysis of PRAT collected at necropsy from people living in Siberia revealed an up to 40% brown adipocyte component.
source: On the other hand, analysis of PRAT collected at necropsy from people living in Siberia revealed an up to 40% BA component, indicating the potential of PRAT to respond to low environmental temperature (Efremova et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: PRAT has the potential to respond to low environmental temperature.
source: On the other hand, analysis of PRAT collected at necropsy from people living in Siberia revealed an up to 40% BA component, indicating the potential of PRAT to respond to low environmental temperature (Efremova et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited study showing increased BA component in cold-exposed populations.

claim: So-called 'dormant' brown adipocytes have been described in PRAT of adult kidney donors, characterized by unilocular morphology, high levels of UCP1 expression, and a gene expression profile that partially overlaps that of white adipocytes.
source: Moreover, so-called 'dormant' BAs have been described in PRAT of adult kidney donors, characterized by unilocular morphology, high levels of UCP1 expression, and a gene expression profile that partially overlaps that of WAs (Jespersen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The process by which brown adipocytes acquire white adipocyte-like properties has been referred to as 'whitening'.
source: The process by which BAs acquire WA-like properties has been referred to as 'whitening', and it is characterized by the enlargement of lipid droplets and reduced expression of thermogenic genes, such as Ucp1 (Shimizu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Whitening is characterized by the enlargement of lipid droplets and reduced expression of thermogenic genes, such as Ucp1.
source: The process by which BAs acquire WA-like properties has been referred to as 'whitening', and it is characterized by the enlargement of lipid droplets and reduced expression of thermogenic genes, such as Ucp1 (Shimizu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Brown-to-white conversion or whitening is a known complication of obesity associated with vascular rarefaction, tissue inflammation, and leptin receptor deficiency.
source: Brown-to-white conversion or whitening is a known complication of obesity associated with vascular rarefaction, tissue inflammation, and leptin receptor deficiency (Kotzbeck et al., 2018; Rangel-Azevedo et al., 2022; Shimizu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Warm adaptation, impaired β-adrenergic signaling, and loss of adipose triglyceride lipase have been implicated in BAT whitening.
source: In addition, warm adaptation, impaired β-adrenergic signaling, and loss of adipose triglyceride lipase have also been implicated in BAT whitening (Kotzbeck et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Under normal physiological conditions, whitening of BAT has only been demonstrated in rabbit iBAT.
source: Under normal physiological conditions, whitening of BAT has only been demonstrated in rabbit iBAT (Huang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A total of 11,708 nuclei were profiled for mPRAT from 1-, 2-, and 6-month-old C57BL/6J male mice.
source: After strict quality control (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C), we profiled a total of 11,708 and 31,079 nuclei for mPRAT and iBAT, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the number of nuclei analyzed in the study.

claim: A total of 31,079 nuclei were profiled for iBAT from 1-, 2-, and 6-month-old C57BL/6J male mice.
source: After strict quality control (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C), we profiled a total of 11,708 and 31,079 nuclei for mPRAT and iBAT, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the number of nuclei analyzed in the study.

claim: Six cell type clusters were identified in the integrated datasets of mPRAT, including adipocyte, ASPC, macrophage, vascular (endothelial cell and pericyte) and mesothelial cells.
source: In the integrated datasets of mPRAT, we identified six clusters based on differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including adipocyte, ASPC, macrophage, vascular (endothelial cell and pericyte) and mesothelial cells that are commonly present in adipose tissue (Massier et al., 2023; Figure 1A and B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the snRNA-seq data analysis and shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: mPRAT was mostly composed of adipocytes and the relative proportions of all the cell types remained largely unchanged during the analyzed time points.
source: mPRAT was mostly composed of adipocytes and the relative proportions of all the cell types remained largely unchanged during the analyzed time points (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Similar cell types and cellular composition were identified in the integrated datasets of iBAT, with the exception of the presence of smooth muscle cells and absence of mesothelial cells.
source: Similar cell types and cellular composition were identified in the integrated datasets of iBAT, with the exception of the presence of smooth muscle cells and absence of mesothelial cells (Figure 1D–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This is supported by the snRNA-seq data analysis and shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: Adipocytes in murine mPRAT were highly heterogeneous and could be separated into four interconnected subpopulations.
source: Adipocytes in murine mPRAT were highly heterogeneous and could be separated into four interconnected subpopulations, all expressing the Plin1 gene that encodes the lipid droplet protein Perilipin, which we referred to as mPRAT-ad1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (Figure 1G and H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by the snRNA-seq data analysis and shown in Figure 1G and H.

claim: mPRAT-ad1 resembled classical brown adipocytes and expressed Ucp1, Cidea, Pank1, and Gk.
source: mPRAT-ad1 resembled classical BAs and expressed Ucp1, Cidea, Pank1, and Gk (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: mPRAT-ad2 was characterized by the expression of Cidea, Pank1, and Gk, but not Ucp1.
source: mPRAT-ad2 was characterized by the expression of Cidea, Pank1, and Gk, but not Ucp1 (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: mPRAT-ad2 expressed detectable levels of Cyp2e1 and Slit3.
source: In addition, it also expressed detectable levels of Cyp2e1 and Slit3 (Figure 1H and I), two genes which have recently been implicated in thermogenesis regulation (Sun et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: Cyp2e1 and Slit3 have recently been implicated in thermogenesis regulation.
source: In addition, it also expressed detectable levels of Cyp2e1 and Slit3 (Figure 1H and I), two genes which have recently been implicated in thermogenesis regulation (Sun et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: mPRAT-ad2 may contain BA-like cells that could be recruited by stimuli that induce thermogenesis.
source: Such gene expression pattern suggested that mPRAT-ad2 may contain BA-like cells that could be recruited by stimuli that induce thermogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression pattern observed in mPRAT-ad2.

claim: mPRAT-ad3 expressed higher levels of Cyp2e1 and Slit3, lower levels of Tshr and Slc7a10, but not Aldh1a1 or Lep.
source: In contrast, mPRAT-ad3, which expressed higher levels of Cyp2e1 and Slit3, lower levels of Tshr and Slc7a10, but not Aldh1a1 or Lep, and mPRAT-ad4, which expressed Cyp2e1, Slit3, Aldh1a1, Lep, and high levels of Tshr and Slc7a10, more closely resembled classical WAs, of which mPRAT-ad4 would appear to be at a more mature stage (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: mPRAT-ad4 expressed Cyp2e1, Slit3, Aldh1a1, Lep, and high levels of Tshr and Slc7a10.
source: In contrast, mPRAT-ad3, which expressed higher levels of Cyp2e1 and Slit3, lower levels of Tshr and Slc7a10, but not Aldh1a1 or Lep, and mPRAT-ad4, which expressed Cyp2e1, Slit3, Aldh1a1, Lep, and high levels of Tshr and Slc7a10, more closely resembled classical WAs, of which mPRAT-ad4 would appear to be at a more mature stage (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: mPRAT-ad3 and mPRAT-ad4 more closely resembled classical white adipocytes.
source: In contrast, mPRAT-ad3, which expressed higher levels of Cyp2e1 and Slit3, lower levels of Tshr and Slc7a10, but not Aldh1a1 or Lep, and mPRAT-ad4, which expressed Cyp2e1, Slit3, Aldh1a1, Lep, and high levels of Tshr and Slc7a10, more closely resembled classical WAs, of which mPRAT-ad4 would appear to be at a more mature stage (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression patterns observed.

claim: mPRAT-ad4 would appear to be at a more mature stage than mPRAT-ad3.
source: In contrast, mPRAT-ad3, which expressed higher levels of Cyp2e1 and Slit3, lower levels of Tshr and Slc7a10, but not Aldh1a1 or Lep, and mPRAT-ad4, which expressed Cyp2e1, Slit3, Aldh1a1, Lep, and high levels of Tshr and Slc7a10, more closely resembled classical WAs, of which mPRAT-ad4 would appear to be at a more mature stage (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression patterns observed.

claim: Adipocytes of iBAT could be separated into four distinct subpopulations (iBAT-ad1, 2, 3, and 4).
source: Adipocytes of iBAT could also be separated into four distinct subpopulations, which we referred to as iBAT-ad1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by the snRNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1I.

claim: iBAT-ad1, 2, and 3 contained brown adipocytes that expressed different levels of Ucp1 and Cidea.
source: iBAT-ad1, 2, and 3 contained BAs that expressed different levels of Ucp1 and Cidea, and may correspond to previously identified low- and high-thermogenic BA subpopulations (Song et al., 2020; Figure 1—figure supplement 1J–L).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1J-L.

claim: iBAT-ad1, 2, and 3 may correspond to previously identified low- and high-thermogenic BA subpopulations.
source: iBAT-ad1, 2, and 3 contained BAs that expressed different levels of Ucp1 and Cidea, and may correspond to previously identified low- and high-thermogenic BA subpopulations (Song et al., 2020; Figure 1—figure supplement 1J–L).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with cited literature and gene expression data.

claim: iBAT-ad1, 2, and 3 comprised over 90% of the total adipocyte population in iBAT.
source: Altogether, they comprised over 90% of the total adipocyte population in iBAT (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1I.

claim: iBAT-ad4 expressed Cyp2e1, Slit3, Slc7a10, Aldh1a1, and Lep.
source: On the other hand, iBAT-ad4 expressed Cyp2e1, Slit3, Slc7a10, Aldh1a1, and Lep, and module score analysis of signature genes showed it to bear close similarity to the recently identified P4 adipocyte subpopulation that regulates thermogenesis in iBAT (Sun et al., 2020; Figure 1—figure supplement 1M).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1M.

claim: iBAT-ad4 bears close similarity to the recently identified P4 adipocyte subpopulation that regulates thermogenesis in iBAT.
source: On the other hand, iBAT-ad4 expressed Cyp2e1, Slit3, Slc7a10, Aldh1a1, and Lep, and module score analysis of signature genes showed it to bear close similarity to the recently identified P4 adipocyte subpopulation that regulates thermogenesis in iBAT (Sun et al., 2020; Figure 1—figure supplement 1M).
evidence: This is supported by module score analysis and citation to prior literature.

claim: mPRAT-ad1 was more similar to all iBAT BA subpopulations (iBAT-ad1, 2, and 3).
source: Comparison between mPRAT and iBAT adipocyte transcriptomes using module score analysis revealed that mPRAT-ad1 was more similar to all iBAT BA subpopulations (iBAT-ad1, 2, and 3), while mPRAT-ad3 and 4 were more similar to iBAT-ad4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1N).
evidence: This is supported by module score analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1N.

claim: mPRAT-ad3 and 4 were more similar to iBAT-ad4.
source: Comparison between mPRAT and iBAT adipocyte transcriptomes using module score analysis revealed that mPRAT-ad1 was more similar to all iBAT BA subpopulations (iBAT-ad1, 2, and 3), while mPRAT-ad3 and 4 were more similar to iBAT-ad4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1N).
evidence: This is supported by module score analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1N.

claim: A match for mPRAT-ad2 could not be found among iBAT adipocytes.
source: Interestingly, we could not find a match for mPRAT-ad2 among iBAT adipocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1N), suggesting that it represents a distinct subpopulation of adipocytes specific to mPRAT, but absent in classical BAT.
evidence: This is supported by module score analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1N.

claim: mPRAT-ad2 represents a distinct subpopulation of adipocytes specific to mPRAT, but absent in classical BAT.
source: Interestingly, we could not find a match for mPRAT-ad2 among iBAT adipocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1N), suggesting that it represents a distinct subpopulation of adipocytes specific to mPRAT, but absent in classical BAT.
evidence: This is an inference based on the module score analysis.

claim: A gradual decrease in the proportions of mPRAT-ad1 (43.0, 34.9, and 33.1% at 1, 2, and 6 months, respectively) and ad2 (36.1, 31.2, and 23.9%, respectively) was observed.
source: Closer inspection of mPRAT adipocyte composition at 1, 2, and 6 mo revealed a gradual decrease in the proportions of mPRAT subpopulations ad1 (43.0, 34.9, and 33.1%, respectively) and ad2 (36.1, 31.2, and 23.9%, respectively), which was accompanied by a reciprocal increase in ad3 (14.7, 26.8, and 29.9%, respectively) and ad4 (6.2, 7.1, and 13.1%, respectively) (Figure 1G), suggesting the existence of a progressive transition in the adipocyte composition of mPRAT during postnatal life.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: A reciprocal increase in mPRAT-ad3 (14.7, 26.8, and 29.9% at 1, 2, and 6 months, respectively) and ad4 (6.2, 7.1, and 13.1%, respectively) was observed.
source: Closer inspection of mPRAT adipocyte composition at 1, 2, and 6 mo revealed a gradual decrease in the proportions of mPRAT subpopulations ad1 (43.0, 34.9, and 33.1%, respectively) and ad2 (36.1, 31.2, and 23.9%, respectively), which was accompanied by a reciprocal increase in ad3 (14.7, 26.8, and 29.9%, respectively) and ad4 (6.2, 7.1, and 13.1%, respectively) (Figure 1G), suggesting the existence of a progressive transition in the adipocyte composition of mPRAT during postnatal life.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The changes in mPRAT adipocyte composition suggest the existence of a progressive transition in the adipocyte composition of mPRAT during postnatal life.
source: Closer inspection of mPRAT adipocyte composition at 1, 2, and 6 mo revealed a gradual decrease in the proportions of mPRAT subpopulations ad1 (43.0, 34.9, and 33.1%, respectively) and ad2 (36.1, 31.2, and 23.9%, respectively), which was accompanied by a reciprocal increase in ad3 (14.7, 26.8, and 29.9%, respectively) and ad4 (6.2, 7.1, and 13.1%, respectively) (Figure 1G), suggesting the existence of a progressive transition in the adipocyte composition of mPRAT during postnatal life.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed changes in adipocyte subpopulation proportions.

claim: Monocle 3 trajectory analysis revealed a single continuous trajectory linking the four mPRAT adipocyte subpopulations.
source: This possibility was further investigated by Monocle 3 trajectory analysis of these cells, which revealed a single continuous trajectory linking the four subpopulations (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by the trajectory analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Pseudo-time values increased steadily from mPRAT-ad1 to mPRAT-ad4.
source: Based on the pattern of composition changes observed through time (Figure 1G), we defined mPRAT-ad1 subpopulation as the starting point of the trajectory uncovering pseudo-time values that increased steadily from mPRAT-ad1 to mPRAT-ad4 (Figure 1J and K).
evidence: This is supported by the trajectory analysis shown in Figure 1J and K.

claim: Along the pseudo-timeline, BA module genes such as Ucp1, Cidea, Ppargc1b, Gk, and Pank1 showed decreasing expression levels.
source: Along the pseudo-timeline, BA module genes such as Ucp1, Cidea, Ppargc1b, Gk, and Pank1 showed decreasing expression levels, whereas WA module genes such as Npr3, Aldh1a1, Tshr, Slc7a10, Slit3, and Cyp2e1 showed the opposite trend (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data along the trajectory shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Along the pseudo-timeline, WA module genes such as Npr3, Aldh1a1, Tshr, Slc7a10, Slit3, and Cyp2e1 showed increasing expression levels.
source: Along the pseudo-timeline, BA module genes such as Ucp1, Cidea, Ppargc1b, Gk, and Pank1 showed decreasing expression levels, whereas WA module genes such as Npr3, Aldh1a1, Tshr, Slc7a10, Slit3, and Cyp2e1 showed the opposite trend (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data along the trajectory shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Gene ontology enrichment analysis revealed a progressive transition from catabolic to anabolic processes along the pseudo-time trajectory.
source: Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis of these genes revealed a progressive transition from catabolic to anabolic processes along the pseudo-time trajectory (Figure 1L).
evidence: This is supported by the GO analysis shown in Figure 1L.

claim: The midpoint of the trajectory, corresponding to the mPRAT-ad2 subpopulation, coincided with the highest expression levels of lipogenic genes, including Acly and Acaca.
source: The midpoint of the trajectory, corresponding to the mPRAT-ad2 subpopulation, coincided with the highest expression levels of lipogenic genes, including Acly and Acaca, as well as enrichment in several synthetic pathways (Figure 1K and L).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data shown in Figure 1K and L.

claim: A similar analysis on iBAT adipocytes failed to reveal a distinct trajectory.
source: A similar analysis on iBAT adipocytes failed to reveal a distinct trajectory and its pseudo-time length of up to 12.8 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1O) was much shorter than that found in mPRAT adipocytes, which reached 26.7 (Figure 1J), suggesting a less heterogeneous and more stable adipocyte population in iBAT.
evidence: This is supported by the trajectory analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1O.

claim: The pseudo-time length of iBAT adipocytes (up to 12.8) was much shorter than that found in mPRAT adipocytes (26.7).
source: A similar analysis on iBAT adipocytes failed to reveal a distinct trajectory and its pseudo-time length of up to 12.8 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1O) was much shorter than that found in mPRAT adipocytes, which reached 26.7 (Figure 1J), suggesting a less heterogeneous and more stable adipocyte population in iBAT.
evidence: This is supported by the trajectory analysis shown in Figure 1J and Figure 1—figure supplement 1O.

claim: The shorter pseudo-time length in iBAT suggests a less heterogeneous and more stable adipocyte population in iBAT.
source: A similar analysis on iBAT adipocytes failed to reveal a distinct trajectory and its pseudo-time length of up to 12.8 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1O) was much shorter than that found in mPRAT adipocytes, which reached 26.7 (Figure 1J), suggesting a less heterogeneous and more stable adipocyte population in iBAT.
evidence: This is an inference based on the trajectory analysis results.

claim: These results suggested the occurrence of a brown-to-white transition during postnatal development in adipocytes of mouse mPRAT.
source: Taken together, these results suggested the occurrence of a brown-to-white transition during postnatal development in adipocytes of mouse mPRAT.
evidence: This is an inference based on the trajectory analysis and gene expression patterns.

claim: Re-clustering of mPRAT ASPC population revealed three subpopulations (mPRAT-aspc1 to 3) that shared the expression of the ASPC marker gene Pdgfra.
source: Re-clustering of mPRAT ASPC population revealed three subpopulations (referred to as mPRAT-aspc1 to 3, respectively) that shared the expression of the ASPC marker gene Pdgfra (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by the re-clustering analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: mPRAT-aspc1 (expressing Dpp4, Pi16, Anxa3) was identified as fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs).
source: mPRAT-aspc1 (expressing Dpp4, Pi16, Anxa3) was identified as fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs), while mPRAT-aspc2 (expressing Pdgfrb and low levels of Pparg) and mPRAT-aspc3 (expressing high levels of Pparg, Cd36, Cidea) represented preadipocytes at different stages of differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is based on gene expression patterns shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: mPRAT-aspc2 (expressing Pdgfrb and low levels of Pparg) and mPRAT-aspc3 (expressing high levels of Pparg, Cd36, Cidea) represented preadipocytes at different stages of differentiation.
source: mPRAT-aspc1 (expressing Dpp4, Pi16, Anxa3) was identified as fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs), while mPRAT-aspc2 (expressing Pdgfrb and low levels of Pparg) and mPRAT-aspc3 (expressing high levels of Pparg, Cd36, Cidea) represented preadipocytes at different stages of differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
